name: unity-dev
description: Unity 6 game development, sixty-two load-by-situation skills covering the whole loop from an empty project to a verified artifact. Every stage — terminal & search: unity-cli (the CLI's surface, exit codes that say whether a retry is honest, MCP wiring, the warm shell), unity-search (a 'find / where is / what references X' question turned into one Unity Search query — asset type filters, folders, labels, ref= relationships, scene component queries — written out before it runs, and opened in a live Editor when one is reachable; read-only, it never selects, moves or edits a result). Concept: unity-game-brief (the first hour, before any Unity work: one line of idea into a one-page experience brief, the look locked with images, an architecture proposal derived from the stated constraints — simulation/presentation split, seeded generation, floating origin — readiness written as testable invariants, then ONE interaction the human can play and react to; to see the game before code, a timed simulated-gameplay preview composited from the game's own rule constants with every sound logged as an event, and a reel with title cards, music and one loudness; after the first interaction, milestones with gates only the person closes, a decision log and a brief for each of several agents), unity-new-project (editor pinning, .meta/LFS, UPM deps pinned to annotated tags, IL2CPP/ARM64, asmdef boundaries, and the async/-quit deadlock that makes a headless package install exit 0 and install nothing; engine-free tests run in seconds with no Editor, and an LFS ledger against the quota), unity-gameplay (START HERE for a gameplay request that names no perspective — fingerprints the project from its scenes and prefabs: 2D or 3D, projection, view, movement model, Cinemachine major; routes controls, camera, animation and verification to the skill owning each; genre recipes written as six constraints rather than labels, level metrics derived from the controller's numbers, production stages with exit checks; for racket and bat games, the clip library measured before the simulation's speeds and contact points are set, and a simulation on its own thread with an absolute clock, a triple-buffered snapshot and a JIT warmup before the clock starts). 3C prototype: unity-input (gameplay reads one struct, never a device — an actions asset with keyboard, gamepad and touch schemes, a reader that latches presses in Update and hands each to FixedUpdate once, input buffering, on-screen sticks, pointer and stick aim, grid steps with key repeat, rebinding saved as JSON, and a scripted source that drives the same funnel from a journey test), unity-camera (camera jitter is two clocks disagreeing — find them before touching damping; Cinemachine rigs for 2D follow with a room confiner, pixel-perfect follow, third-person orbit with deocclusion, first person and fixed posts, shake and blends, the 2.x to 3.x name table, a rig builder, a camera probe and a journey that proves a rig holds on every frame), unity-2d-controller (a platformer character asks physics where the ground is and is not simulated by it — rules and collision as two halves that never mix, a kinematic motor with slopes, one-way and moving platforms, coyote time, variable jump, dash and wall jump, gravity and jump velocity derived from apex height and time to apex, free top-down movement with aim split from move, cell steps shown as tweens, the Animator bridge, and journeys that prove apex, coyote and buffer), unity-3d-controller (choose who owns the transform before writing a line of movement — a CharacterController motor that finds ground by its own cast, with slopes, steps and moving platforms, third-person, first-person, top-down and lane-runner controllers reading one input struct, gravity and jump velocity derived from apex height and time to apex and integrated so the apex holds at every frame rate, the Animator bridge, and journeys that prove ramp, step, apex and lane change), unity-animation (the game owns the state and the Animator renders it, for 3D Humanoid and 2D frame-clip characters — one writer per parameter through a bridge, blend trees and sprite state graphs built from script, AnimationEvents and attack windows that survive interruption, override controllers, foot and hand IK, Timeline handover, root motion, and a journey proving the shown state follows the game; a hand-built PlayableGraph whose clip times follow a simulation's ticks, foot-lock and prop IK as Animation Jobs, and motion metrics that count pops), unity-physics-2d (Box2D answered in its own vocabulary, never a PhysX rule with a 2D suffix — a symptom-routed ladder, first match wins, for callbacks that never fire, tunnelling, casts that miss or hit the caster, bodies that sleep or jitter, composite and tilemap colliders and one-way platforms, with a two-sided debug probe and a read-only scene audit), unity-physics-3d (symptom-routed triage, first-match-wins, a two-sided probe), unity-play-harness (build the game so an agent can drive and read it — a one-line probe snapshot readable from a live Editor, Editor.log or a PlayMode test; named situations that boot straight into a moment and wait on a readiness set instead of a sleep; journey tests that sample the probe into a timeline and assert invariants; a feel complaint turned into a repeatable test; velocity read from a delegate so a 2D body, a CharacterController or a grid mover reports through the same key, with 2D situation templates and a 2D never-inside-geometry invariant). Vertical slice — 2D world: unity-2d-level (a level is data with invariants and the Tilemap is one renderer of it — a serialisable level of tile ids, spawn, gate, pickups and entities painted into a fixed stack of six Tilemap layers, runtime tile edits, rooms and doors, chunks stitched into an endless run, Tiled and LDtk import, SpriteShape terrain, seeded generation, and a validator that exits 1 on a pickup the jump cannot reach), unity-2d-grid (the cell map is the truth and the transform is an animation of it — board logic for tactics games and tile puzzles on rectangular, isometric and hexagonal grids as plain C# with no scene: hexagonal offset, axial and cube conversion for Unity's layout, movement range by flood, A* paths, lines of sight, one occupancy map, push rules, turn order, undo, pointer to cell), unity-tilemap (Tile Palettes for rectangular, hexagonal and isometric grids, and RuleTiles generated from a terrain sheet you already have), unity-2d-rendering (draw order is four keys in a fixed priority and z is the last of them — sorting layer, Order in Layer, render queue, distance along the sort axis; SortingGroup, Y-sort for top-down, isometric and hex scenes, the Light2D that does nothing or turns everything black, shadow casters, normal maps, sprite masks, parallax layers, and a sorting audit that lists every tie). Vertical slice — 3D world: unity-3d-level (a greybox is the level with the art missing — a metrics sheet derived from the body and the jump, a greybox built from it and proven by a walk journey, a modular kit on a 1/2/4 m grid with the pivot at a floor corner, prefab structure with an override audit, collision proxies on one World layer, Terrain, spline roads and lanes, URP decals), unity-lighting (a light's mode decides what it can ever light — a symptom-routed ladder, first match wins, over light modes, the bake, light and reflection probes, shadows and the environment on URP, a read-only scene audit that names candidates, a bake that reads lightmap and probe counts back, and the subset a phone can afford), unity-navigation (the agent owns the transform — decide that first). Vertical slice — systems: unity-interaction (detection is chosen by perspective and the contract is the same everywhere — one IInteractable interface, an interactor that keeps one selected target from a trigger list, a cone overlap on a tick, a camera ray, the cell in front or the pointer, one prompt, pickups counted once, switches, gates as state machines that refuse a second press while they move, locked doors, point-and-click hotspots walked to before they are used, and a journey proving a gate opens once), unity-combat (one swing is one damage event and the engine will not enforce it — a DamageInfo struct and a Health receiver with teams, invincibility and death as a state, hit and hurt layers, query hitboxes that own a swing id and a hit list, opened and closed by animation windows that survive interruption, knock-back through the motor, projectiles that cast every step, bullet patterns as data, and a journey proving one swing across two hurtboxes is one event), unity-game-ai (perception on a budget, decisions on a tick, movement by whoever owns the transform — a code state machine, a small behaviour tree, a vision cone as distance, angle and one cast from a shared budget, hearing and memory, patrol and chase through one mover interface over a NavMeshAgent, a 2D motor or cells, 2D pathfinding, wave spawners on a seed, turn-based move scoring, and a journey proving the sentry chases only after it sees), unity-scene-flow (one scene that never unloads owns what must survive a load, and everything else is rebuilt from data — a Boot scene and its services, additive loading with progress and one operation in flight, a game phase machine in which pause is a state, a versioned save with migrations and an atomic write, read from outside Unity by a checker, checkpoints that rebuild, object pools, ScriptableObject config, a save round-trip test and a journey over the phase machine). Vertical slice — UI: unity-game-ui (detects the project's UI system and routes; owns the runtime IMGUI HUD that editor-tooling docs never cover — GUI.matrix scaling, event swallowing, a type scale derived from viewing distance in arcminutes, mixed Latin/CJK font authoring), unity-ui-ugui (the six ways Canvas UI renders nothing, and the Layout Group vs ContentSizeFitter conflict), unity-ui-toolkit (USS is a subset of CSS and an unsupported property is ignored, not an error). Production — assets: art-asset-registry (one append-only ledger per project for every generated 2D and 3D asset — files with sha256, every .blend version included, lineage and links to the art direction, the job that made it and the evidence image, gates and a verdict, a status set by one command as a person's act, what an upstream change left stale, rows printed for manifest.md, and an existing manifest.md adopted read-only), unity-3d-models (a 3D model routed by its source — an image-to-3D GLB, an FBX character, a Blender rig, a purchased pack — inspected, decimated to its class's target before Unity sees it, imported and audited folder by folder against the class's row; a budget is a person's pick from the same asset generated at every preset up to a showcase baseline and seen static in the game scene, never a fixed cap, and anything to be skinned is decimated before it is rigged), unity-rigged-character (the Unity-side contract for a rigged character, whichever route made the FBX — Auto-Rig Pro, a Blender rig, Mixamo, an auto-rig service: the humanoid contract skeleton every motion source maps to through a role map, import, an Avatar that is Generic by default and Humanoid only for a body-part mask or IK, built from an explicit map with the chest and fingers, the Animator, a prop socket kept under Optimize Game Objects, the PBR maps an FBX drops rebuilt, and gameplay volumes authored as constants because no renderer box fits the body), unity-2d-sprites (sprite metadata lives in the importer; a set of frames turned into a playable AnimationClip; the capability gate that prevents silent corruption), unity-2d-animation (a skeletal sprite is a mesh and costs like one — a PSB imported as a character rig, bones then geometry then weights in the Skinning Editor, SpriteSkin bindings and CPU or GPU deformation, Sprite Library skins and equipment swapped through SpriteResolver, IK Manager 2D limbs, and an audit of what a rig costs), unity-2d-pixel-perfect (soft, crawling or seam-ridden pixel art, across both of the components called PixelPerfectCamera), unity-sprite-atlas (V2 atlases from script: the editor/runtime split, packing and platform settings, and how the packed texture reaches the player), unity-audio (load types, sample rates, mixer cost; reports before it reimports), unity-localization (the CJK font pipeline, and the two contradictory standard answers for it). Production — AI asset generation: game-character-pipeline (START HERE for a rigged character made from an image — the quality target, the route and the track decided once: a preview rig on the dense mesh, the ship track's budget, game mesh and one local rig, or the upgrade track a person chooses after the demo, where a paid cloud service remakes only the mesh and the demo's clips carry over; then stages S0–S13, each with the skill that owns it, its entry and exit gates and its artefacts), codex-visual (2D art through the codex image model, held on-style by one art bible and one anchor — grid one-shot sets, animation sheets generated as one grid and sliced into measured frames with a GIF preview, chroma-key transparency, normalised sizes and a geometry gate that reads centre and size back from the shipped files — position and size are never asked of the model; also the four source views of an image-to-3D character, A-pose or T-pose, review sheets composed only when their numeric checks pass, and themed overview sheets of a project's pictures, each cell captioned with its source path and every file's hash recorded; the key colour chosen against the subject before generating, a tint-axis un-mix for a field painted off its declared key, and a breathing idle made from one still that copies every pixel and keeps the head identical), comfyui-asset-generation (music, SFX, MiniMax H3 video and image-to-3D props and characters through a self-hosted ComfyUI — one job at a time, /history as the only proof, /free before a model switch; four views cleaned before upload with the mask polarity checked, the project graph diffed against the official template before any knob moves, generation presets compared as rungs of one ladder, none of them a target; keyframe layout maps drawn from ground coordinates with crossing moves found before anything is generated, and a camera gate that rejects a keyframe whose horizon moved), sprite-from-video (one character still turned into transparent sprite frames through a generated video — the still padded onto an exact-key canvas sized for the motion, an in-place image-to-video clip, every frame keyed against the colour the model actually painted, the loop period found from a frame-distance lag profile with a half-stride guard and a seam gate, or a one-shot cut between rest poses, written as equal-canvas frames and a frames.json), blender-character-rig (an image-to-3D character rigged and animated in a running Blender through its MCP server — bones placed from measured landmarks, skin weights computed by position where bone heat fails on a double shell, an extreme-pose render as the weight test, a prop parented to a hand bone, an FK action keyed in armature axes, contact measured before a render, and an FBX read back by re-import; the same modules run headless as gated stages, fitting one clip pack's skeleton to the mesh and building skinned LODs into a byte-identical FBX), blender-retarget (stock clips onto a rig in Blender, where a rotation key is a turn from its bone's own rest and is converted by conjugation, never copied — Auto-Rig Pro or a pure-bpy bone map, a manifest of clips, a local weight repair, a library with one NLA review track, a prop checked against its hand bone in every clip, and an audit that re-opens the saved file; root translation retargeted by the hip-height ratio and gated when a clip loses it; a measured bake-off between fitting the mesh to the pack's skeleton, Humanoid and per-clip baking, gated on the foot slide a route adds; and one clip's motion metrics — plant slide, penetration, jitter, joint limits, loop seam, root drift, pops that fail), character-autorig (a humanoid mesh rigged locally and headless with the user's own Auto-Rig Pro, never a cloud rigging service — fused limbs and double shells caught before any rig, joint markers measured from slices and shown on front and side pictures for a person, append, Match, bind and a Unity FBX in one call, the result mapped onto the humanoid contract skeleton, and six extreme poses gated on volume loss and self-intersection; a hand-built rig from the same markers as the fallback), humanoid-motion (clips from video onto the humanoid contract with two cameras in one generated frame — a front and a side view of the character animated by a local image-to-video model, read by a reader trained for that character and triangulated straight onto its skeleton, ported from anymove, run by one cross-platform runner that has you look at the take before training; then foot lock baked offline with each foot's sole height, a loop cut, motion-metric gates that tell a pop the video has from one the solve added, and a ledger record carrying the sales territory of the video it came from). Polish & optimisation: unity-game-feel (feedback is a stack per event with a budget, not effects added until it feels right — a Feedback component that plays motion, flash, particles, shake, sound, haptics and time by priority with reduce-motion settings, one owner of Time.timeScale for hit stop, flashes that restore, squash and tweens with no library, pooled SFX with a voice cap, rumble that stops, and a journey proving time comes back after every stop), unity-render-urp (the Volume pre-flight behind 'I set it and nothing happened', the mobile subset, an eight-point Render Graph review), unity-urp-migration (a Built-in project moved to URP in five gated phases, each one read back from the saved project rather than from the converter log — magenta materials and the 2D shader hijack, PPv2 into a Volume profile that survives a reload, lightmaps that are still Built-in data, GrabPass/OnRenderImage/surface shaders, and the four traps that let a half-moved project look done), unity-profiling (the work behind a slow or uneven frame as numbers an agent can compare across changes — ProfilerRecorder counters without the Profiler window, 90-frame windows with median/p95/worst, scheduled/completed/discarded work counters for streaming and pooling, and a before/after table; a driven run is not a hardware benchmark), unity-scene-optimisation (optimise the counter that moved, not the one you remember — batching paths read in the Frame Debugger, LODGroup and Mesh LOD, baked and GPU occlusion culling, per-layer cull distances, texture size and mipmap streaming, sprite and particle overdraw, each with a one-window test that shows whether its lever can move the counter at all, and a read-only scene cost audit), unity-debug (CHECK THE INSTRUMENT FIRST — stale results files and settings assets that were never in effect; four loops, the fastest driving a LIVE Editor in sub-second round trips against ~20 s for batchmode; Safe Mode's deadlock). Shipping: unity-device-testing (acceptance on a REAL Android or iOS phone from a terminal — a probe scene that logs one tagged line per state change, an adb/devicectl driver that asserts on those lines and taps system dialogs by focus and rotation, a human asked for one physical action at a time and verified from the device, and exit codes that keep a real failure apart from a broken harness), unity-android-release (build it then PROVE it — a driver that refuses rather than warns, reading the artifact back with aapt/apksigner, per-build provenance), unity-ios-build (from a Unity project to a process on an iPhone without opening Xcode — headless build, an unsigned compile gate, signing with what the Mac actually holds and why the id in a certificate's name is not the team, devicectl install and the console as the only log channel, and a native .mm plugin iterated in 30 seconds instead of six minutes), unity-web-release (the server headers that undo every Unity setting, and iOS Safari's memory ceiling). Backend & commerce: unity-live-services, unity-monetization, unity-multiplayer, and the API layer they hand off to — unity-ugs (which package provides what, the initialisation order everything else depends on, Cloud Save access classes, Cloud Code, Remote Config, the Deployment Window file types), unity-iap (In-App Purchasing v5 call by call: store connection, the pending/confirm flow, receipts, entitlement, restore), unity-ads-levelplay (LevelPlay mediation: native dependency resolution, consent before init, rewarded/interstitial/banner units, impression-level revenue), unity-multiplayer-services (the Sessions API: join codes, a browsable game list, quick join, ticket matchmaking, relay, host migration, dedicated servers), unity-vivox (voice and text chat: sign-in, group/echo/positional channels, the roster, mute and push-to-talk, microphone permission). Install in Unity projects.
